adjudication: Fresh independent semantic scope review of the specified iteration-05 borderline cases only
basis: Fixed actual questions, unchanged v9 key, grading-scope-policy-v2.json, whole same-question answers including all evidence fields, summary snapshot and authoritative extracted/PDF Law. No other iterations, grades, reviews, adjudications, or reader communication consulted. PDF wording independently verified with pypdf, physical pages as indicated.

cases.question: How do crafting costs, repeat use of crafting pieces, absent supply items and duplicate persistent effects work?
cases.reasoning: The fixed question expressly asks how duplicate persistent effects work. The restriction is ownership-specific: an identical effect in the crafting player's own play area prevents another, whereas an identical effect belonging to another player does not. “Cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in play” leaves this material scope unresolved and on its natural unrestricted reading extends the ban to other players. Nothing else in this same-ID answer or its evidence labels supplies “your play area.” This is an additional valid incomplete-scope finding, distinct from the stipulated omission of ordinary crafting pieces deriving their suit from their clearing. Recommend partial for the unresolved qualifier; do not upgrade this shorthand to a definite explicit assertion that another player's effect blocks crafting. A clear global prohibition would instead be a wrong material ruling. Persistent-card destination is contextual under the prospective policy, but the ownership qualifier to the expressly asked duplicate prohibition is not merely destination context.

answer.part: craft cost; reuse; absent item; duplicate persistent effect
answer.ruling: Bottom-left icons define cost. Marquise/Eyrie/Alliance activate one matching-suit workshop/roost/sympathy for each icon, each piece once per turn. Vagabond exhausts one face-up undamaged hammer per icon and current clearing must match every icon; may activate repeatedly. Three-color ? accepts any suit. Item card cannot be crafted unless corresponding item token is in map supply. Cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in play.
answer.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1)

reader_wording.evidence: Actions > Shared movement, crafting and battle; Craft (4.1)

fixed_key.expected_answer: Activate crafting pieces matching every crafting icon; each piece may normally activate only once per turn. A crafting piece's suit is its clearing's suit, and the card's own suit is not its crafting cost. An item must be available in the map supply or that card cannot be crafted. Resolve an immediate effect and discard the card; a persistent effect stays in the play area, and an identical persistent effect already there prevents crafting another. For Vagabond crafting, exhaust one face-up, undamaged hammer per crafting icon; the pawn may be activated repeatedly, but its clearing must match every crafting icon. Reusing the pawn does not waive the hammer payment for each icon.

source_refs.wording: You cannot craft a persistent effect if you have an identical one in your play area.
A crafting piece’s suit matches its clearing.

support.wording: The ordinary crafting-piece suit is the suit of its clearing. “You cannot craft an identical persistent effect already in your play area.”

cases.question: How do Vagabond Explore, Quest and Repair work, including costs, rewards and item sides?
cases.reasoning: The whole answer resolves every fixed-key Explore, Quest and Repair step, quantity, reward and item-side requirement. Its Quest clause includes matching clearing, exhausting the two listed items, completion, both reward alternatives including this quest, and replacement. The exact authoritative 9.5.5 says “Choose a quest whose suit matches your clearing”; it does not say “face-up.” The fixed key likewise has no face-up-display target. Initial face-up display is setup in 9.3.3; the summary helpfully makes that selection context explicit. Do not silently add a new expected face-up-display restriction to this unchanged key or treat the item-sides wording in the question as a separate request about quest-card visibility. There is no affirmative permission here to choose an unseen deck quest. If an evaluator wants display-only selection as an additional mandatory broad-procedure target, that is a prospective key/scope completeness decision, not an existing reader error demonstrated by 9.5.5.

answer.ruling: Explore exhaust torch in ruin clearing, take hidden item face up into Satchel/track and score 1 VP if item taken; remove ruin when last item taken. Quest in matching clearing: exhaust its 2 listed items, complete it, choose VP equal to completed matching quests including this one or draw 2 cards, then draw replacement quest. Repair exhaust hammer and move 1 damaged item to Satchel keeping its face; ready tea/coins/bags move to tracks if space.

fixed_key.expected_answer: Explore exhaust torch for item beneath ruin in clearing; take face up, score one VP if item taken, remove ruin after last item. Quest matches clearing suit, exhaust two listed items, complete quest, choose VP equal matching completed quests including this or draw two; replace quest. Repair exhaust hammer to move damaged item to satchel keeping its face; face-up tea/coins/bags move to matching track if able.

source_refs.wording: Choose a quest whose suit matches your clearing, and exhaust the two items listed on the quest. Place the quest in your play area as a completed quest. Then, you may either score one victory point per matching completed quest (including this) or draw two cards from the deck. Finally, draw a new quest and place it near the map.
Shuffle your quest deck, draw 3 quest cards, and place them face up near you.
Explore takes the ruin item face up and scores one point if an item is taken; Repair keeps the damaged item on its current side.

support.wording: The summary explicitly supplies all answered Explore/Quest/Repair details. It additionally says “Choose a face-up quest matching clearing”; that extra display wording is not a separate target in the frozen key.

cases.key_completeness_concern: Display-only quest selection could be made explicit in a future key if intended as mandatory; it must not be retroactively invented as a target in this adjudication. Exact Law 9.5.5 is not evidence that the phrase face-up appears there.

cases.question: What is Vagabond Aid cost and target, is a crafted item required, and how are repeated Aid relationship improvements counted?
cases.reasoning: The question specifically asks how repeated Aid relationship improvements are counted. Same-turn accumulation and one improvement per Aid are correctly stated, but “required number of times” does not identify what determines that number. The fixed key requires the printed Aid count per step; Law 9.2.9.Ia and the summary resolve it as the number between the current and next relationship spaces. This is not a request to memorize all track values, nor an insistence on the literal verb “printed”: any semantic identification of the step-specific threshold would suffice. This same-ID answer and its evidence labels identify neither the threshold source nor numerical values, so a requested counting fact remains unresolved. Advancement VP remains contextual under policy Q53 and is not another deduction.

answer.ruling: Exhaust one face-up undamaged item of any type and give a card matching clearing to a player with faction pieces there, even Hostile; may then take a crafted item from their Crafted Items if available, but none required to Aid. Non-Hostile relationship advances only when Aid that faction required number of times in same turn; each Aid counts toward one improvement.

fixed_key.expected_answer: Exhaust any ready undamaged item, give matching clearing card to player with faction pieces there. May take crafted item if present, but Aid can occur without item. For non-hostile faction meet printed Aid count within same turn per step, each Aid counts once toward one improvement; advance and score new space.

source_refs.wording: Aid a non-Hostile faction the number of times listed between their current Allied space and their next Allied space during the same turn. (A given Aid action counts toward only one improvement in relationship.)
Exhaust any one item and give a card matching your clearing to a player with faction pieces there (even Hostile).

support.wording: The summary supplies Aid payment/target/optional item and says to Aid as many times in this same turn as printed between current and next spaces; one Aid counts toward only one improvement.

cases.question: Can Vagabond craft a card requiring fox and rabbit icons from one clearing, reuse the pawn for multiple craftings, and immediately use a crafted item?
cases.reasoning: The actual fixed question asks three capabilities: mixed-suit crafting from one clearing, repeated pawn activation, and immediate crafted-item use. All three are explicitly and correctly resolved. Repetition is permitted despite the once-per-turn limit, with one hammer required for each icon, and immediate use is conditioned on costs and requirements. The source/key also explain the hammer-exhaustion procedure. B does not explicitly name that operation here, and an evidence heading alone should not import an absent procedural fact. However, the fixed question does not ask how to pay crafting costs or describe the full crafting procedure; the omitted verb is therefore contextual procedural detail rather than a missing requested capability. “Each icon requires its own hammer” is compatible with exhaustion and does not claim that hammers remain ready or that costs are waived. Do not infer an explicit free-reuse ruling. A broad crafting-cost question would require exhaustion and this wording alone would then be incomplete. This scope judgment does not use another answer ID to fill anything.

answer.part: Can Vagabond craft a card requiring fox and rabbit icons from one clearing, reuse the pawn for multiple craftings, and immediately use a crafted item?
answer.ruling: No: the pawn's current clearing must match every crafting icon, so one clearing cannot pay mixed fox/rabbit requirements. Vagabond may activate its pawn repeatedly despite the normal once-per-turn crafting limit, but each icon requires its own hammer. When crafting an item, Vagabond may immediately take it face up into Satchel/track and use it for another Daylight action immediately if costs and other requirements are met; the item must be in supply to craft.

fixed_key.expected_answer: Cannot satisfy mixed suits because clearing must match every icon. Each icon exhausts hammer, pawn may activate repeatedly ignoring once/turn cap. Crafted item can immediately be taken face up, usable if otherwise eligible.

source_refs.wording: The Vagabond can exhaust H to activate its pawn as a crafting piece, ignoring the once-per-turn limit (4.1.1). If the Vagabond crafts an item, he may immediately take it, face up.
Craft a card by exhausting one H per crafting icon it has. Your clearing must match all of the card’s crafting icons.
The Vagabond exhausts face-up undamaged items, flipping them face down, to take many actions.

support.wording: The summary supplies the mixed-suit prohibition, repeat activation, one-hammer-per-icon payment, and immediate usable acquisition with action costs and requirements. It also explicitly supplies exhaustion, which is available context but is not claimed to appear in this reader wording.

cases.key_completeness_concern: No defect in the key rule. The key contains extra procedural explanation beyond the three capability clauses; its presence alone does not create a fourth requested clause.

cases.question: How many Daylight actions may the Vagabond take, must the action types follow a fixed order, and may the same action type be repeated?
cases.reasoning: The fixed question asks the general Daylight action allowance, fixed ordering, and repeatability. The answer resolves all three: any number constrained by eligible items, no fixed order, and repeated types allowed. This is the general rule stated in 9.5 itself. Ranger Hideout is a separate character action effect that immediately ends Daylight. It is true, present in the summary, and helpfully appended in the key, but the fixed question neither names Hideout/Ranger nor requests character-specific termination exceptions or the Special action procedure. Treating that appended key sentence as another mandatory clause would expand the actual question. The answer does not explicitly permit continuing after Hideout. “Any order and number” in the general phase rule is not such a contrary ruling; otherwise the authoritative 9.5 preamble itself would be defective. No same-ID evidence imports the absent exception, and no other ID is needed: it is unasked context, not a semantically supplied exception.

answer.ruling: Daylight actions may be taken in any order and number as ready undamaged items permit; action types can be repeated.

fixed_key.expected_answer: The Vagabond may take Daylight actions in any order and number, repeating or interleaving action types as desired, provided each action can pay its item costs and meet its other requirements. There is no separate fixed action-count allowance. Ranger Hideout still immediately ends Daylight as specified.

source_refs.wording: You can exhaust items to take the following actions, in any order and number.
The Vagabond exhausts face-up undamaged items, flipping them face down, to take many actions.
Exhaust one F to repair three items. Then, immediately end Daylight and begin Evening.

support.wording: Daylight is “Any order/number, as ready undamaged items permit.” A separate Ranger character row states Hideout immediately ends Daylight and begins Evening.

cases.key_completeness_concern: The key correctly includes Hideout context; no key change is needed to grade the actual general allowance/order/repetition question. An explicit post-Hideout continuation claim would be incorrect.
